structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Secure rugged edge-processing integration, U.S.-designed/manufactured motherboard capability and defense qualification create switching friction, but commercial silicon and competing defense integrators limit exclusivity.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Defense modernization supports demand, but program timing and customer procurement concentration make conversion uneven.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Qualification/security requirements raise replacement friction, while alternative qualified embedded-compute suppliers and primes remain substitutes.

discovery-weak-signals.name: defense electronics demand visibility
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Record bookings and backlog provide forward demand evidence across Mercury's defense electronics portfolio.

adversarial-red-team.name: financialOperatingMomentum
adversarial-red-team.basis: Revenue/bookings/backlog improved strongly, but GAAP profitability and year-over-year cash conversion remain weaker than adjusted operating measures imply.

expectations-execution.name: operating recovery versus cash conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA improved materially while quarterly free cash flow weakened.

items.risk: Defense program timing and customer concentration can make backlog conversion uneven.
If cash conversion does not recover alongside backlog growth, earnings-quality expectations should be tempered.
Backlog is demand visibility, not guaranteed margin or cash conversion; program timing and execution remain material.
Adjusted EBITDA growth can overstate economic recovery if working-capital intensity, program charges or cash conversion remain weak.
Defense customer/program concentration and procurement timing can delay backlog conversion.
Commercial compute advances can reduce differentiation unless Mercury sustains security, qualification and integration advantages.
